parts.text: Explain how IUCN Red List™ assessments help to conserve biodiversity.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 6.1 and the IUCN assessments for P. arion, suggest how the abundance of the butterfly differs across its distribution.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
P. arion has been successfully re-introduced in the United Kingdom at 12 sites. These sites were restored to flower-rich grassland.

The conservation management actions designed for P. arion also resulted in the re-establishment or increase of other species at the restored sites. These included 12 species of flowering plant, 8 other butterfly species and 4 species of other insects.
parts.text: Use the information given to suggest why P. arion went extinct in the United Kingdom in 1979.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Outline the advantages of restoring habitats for endangered species.
